text.p: Russia's Vera Ilyina drew on her vast experience to snatch victory with her last dive and retain her European one-metre springboard title on Friday.

Ilyina, silver medallist on the three-metre board at the 1994 world championships, overhauled German Doerte Lindner with her fifth and last effort to take her European medal tally to three golds, two silvers and one bronze.

Fellow Russian Irina Lashko, an equally seasoned competitor who won the inaugurual European one-metre title in 1989 and the three-metre crown in 1991, pipped Lindner for the silver with the last dive of the final.
Ilyina, who won both the one-metre and three-metre titles at the last European championships in 1995, compiled 268.14 points.
Lashko scored 264.72 and Lindner, who took the lead from Ilyina in the second round and held it to the last, 264.36.
It was Russia's second gold of the day following the fourth consecutive European success of Olga Sedakova in the synchronised swimming solo event.
